amarilla, de fruto carnoso y la de forma de pera, importa
da recientemente . De berenjenas , la apepinada y la listada .
Los

excerpts.translation:
240
Peppers, Tomatoes and Eggplants.-It is the most important group among vegetables. The cultivation of the tomato becomes more widespread each year, employing great care, harvested in all seasons, thanks to the benignity of the climate. The pepper is also cultivated on a fairly large scale, but tends to decrease, and the cultivation of the eggplant is dedicated only to small plots.
The markets for the first two species, apart from local consumption, are all of Spain, being sold in Madrid with great esteem. Additionally, they are shipped to Barcelona, Marseille, and Melilla.
The varieties of pepper are the ball, guindilla, the long encarnado, the sweet square, and the cornuzuelo. Varieties of tomatoes: the country variety, with thin and lustrous skin; the yellow, with fleshy fruit, and the pear-shaped variety, recently imported. Of eggplants, the apepinada and the striped.
The residues of this group have the same utilization as those of group C (melon, watermelon, cucumber, and squash).
Intense cold causes crop losses and delays in the vegetation of the plants, and to avoid this, shelters of reeds and siscas or saddles are placed, inclined over the lines.

La calabaza reviste más importancia que las anteriores
especies citadas, consumiéndose en gran escala como ali
mento del hombre, y también del ganado de cerda.
Apio y Perejil.-Ofrecen ambas poco interés en la pro
vincia, cultivándose en muchas huertas, pero en pequeña
escala, por el escaso consumo que de ellas se hace, no lle
gando á formar tablas, sino algunas líneas solamente .
Pimiento, Tomate y Berenjena .—De las tres especies que
figuran en este grupo , las dos primeras son las que mayor
importancia alcanzan en las huertas de la provincia, exce
diendo su área de cultivo á todas las demás, y siendo ob
jeto de gran consumo.
El pimiento , de cultivo muy generalizado , tiene su prin
cipal asiento en la huerta de la capital , donde ocupa ta
blares de bastante consideración , destinándose el fruto al
consumo directo en estado fresco y á la fabricación de con
servas .
El tomate se emplea en las mismas aplicaciones que el
pimiento, hallándose también muy extendido, sobre todo
en los términos de Bullalbufar, Puigpuñent, Sóller , Vallde
mosa, etc.
La berenjena se cultiva en menor escala que las dos an
teriores especies, y casi siempre en las huertas que circun
dan las grandes poblaciones .
260
Alcachofa, Lechuga y Escurola.-Son estas las únicas es
pecies que se explotan de este grupo. La primera se halla
poco extendida en la provincia, desarrollándose general
mente en tierras de secano.
La lechuga tiene interés secundario, por lo que sólo se
cultiva en la proximidad de las grandes poblaciones á cau
sa de la naturaleza de su aprovechamiento y reducidas
aplicaciones.
El cultivo de la escarola todavía es menos importante
que el anterior, siendo análogas sus aplicaciones.
Acelgas, Fspinacas y Rábanos . -Las tres especies vege
tales que se han comprendido en este grupo están muy
poco generalizadas en armonía con el exiguo consumo que
de ellas se hace . Los rábanos tienen alguna mayor impor
tancia, pero raras veces llegan á destinárseles tablares ex
profeso, sino que se intercalan entre otras plantas.
Todas las hortalizas de la provincia se consumen en los
mismos centros productores, especialmente en la capital,
con la sola excepción del tomate, cuyo sobrante se envía
á Barcelona, aunque en pequeña
escala , siendo principal
mente la comarca exportadora la formada por el término
de Bullalbufar y pueblos colindantes .
El aprovechamiento de los residuos de las hortalizas
producidas en la provincia se reduce generalmente á las
hojas exteriores y tallos y algunas plantas faltas de condi
ciones para concurrir al mercado . Estos residuos se des
tinan de ordinario á la alimentación de los gan

not very widespread, consumption being also limited.
The pumpkin is of greater importance than the aforementioned
species, being consumed on a large scale as food for humans, and also for pigs.
Celery and Parsley.-These two offer little interest in the
province, being cultivated in many market gardens, but on a small
scale, due to the limited consumption made of them, not
forming tables, but only a few lines.
Pepper, Tomato and Aubergine.-Of the three species
that appear in this group, the first two are those of greatest
importance in the province's market gardens, exceeding in cultivation area all the others, and being the subject of great consumption.
The pepper, very widely cultivated, has its main location in the market garden of the capital, where it occupies tables of considerable size, the fruit being destined for direct consumption in fresh state and for the manufacture of preserves.
The tomato is used in the same applications as the
pepper, being also very widespread, especially
in the areas of Bullalbufar, Puigpuñent, Sóller, Vallde
mosa, etc.
The aubergine is cultivated on a smaller scale than the two
previous species, and almost always in the market gardens surrounding the large towns.
260
Artichoke, Lettuce and Endive.-These are the only species
exploited from this group. The first is not very widespread in the province, generally developing in dryland fields.
Lettuce has secondary interest, and is therefore only
cultivated near large towns due to the nature of its use and limited
applications.
The cultivation of endive is even less important
than the previous one, its applications being similar.
Chards, Spinach and Radishes.-The three vegetable species
included in this group are very
little widespread in accordance with the meagre consumption made of them. Radishes have somewhat greater
importance, but tables are rarely dedicated exclusively to them, but rather they are interspersed among other plants.
All the vegetables of the province are consumed in the
same production centres, especially in the capital, with the sole exception of the tomato, whose surplus is sent
to Barcelona, although on a small
scale, the main exporting area being formed by the municipality
of Bullalbufar and neighbouring towns.
The use of vegetable residues produced in the province is generally limited to the outer leaves and stems and some plants lacking the
conditions to be offered at the market. These residues are usually
destined for the feeding of livestock

talizas de la provincia es la sequía originada por la falta

También les son nocivos los fríos tempranos y tardíos y

resintiéndose algunas de los excesivos calores, y causando

en verano. Las lluvias persistentes de otoño en nada favo

en calidad.
También sufren las hortalizas los ataques de algunos in

que ocasiona el grilio-talpa , vulgarmente llamado Cudell,
el cual destruye las raíces de las plantas que encuentra al
abrir las galerías .

The weather accident that most harms the vegetable
patches of the province is the drought caused by the lack
of rain or its poor distribution, with the scarcity of
water for irrigation being the main cause of the poor har
30
vests.
They are also harmed by early and late frosts and
fog, especially affecting cabbages, peppers, and tomatoes,
with some suffering from excessive heat, and causing
serious damage to all from hailstones that usually fall
in summer. Persistent autumn rains in no way fav
our lettuce and endives, causing them to deteriorate
in quality.
Vegetables also suffer attacks from some in
sects, distinguished among all by the serious damage
caused by the mole cricket, commonly called Cudell,
which destroys the roots of the plants it finds when
opening the galleries.

, the most frequent, although it presents with little intensity due to lack of moisture, is the oidium of the cucurbits Sphaerotheca humuli. To combat or prevent this disease, sulfur application has been recommended, but its use has hardly been carried out due to the minor importance of this pest.
From group D, Parsley is cultivated only on a very limited extent.
The group that offers the greatest importance in this province is constituted by Pepper, Tomato, and Eggplant, and that is due to the extent dedicated to the cultivation of the tomato, since from the pepper and eggplants, only 92 hectares of the former and 6 of the latter are cultivated, while 1,730 hectares of tomato are cultivated, constituting, after the banana, the most widespread cultivation in the Irrigated Zone.
It began to be established on the islands of Tenerife and Gran Canaria, occupying mainly the coast of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Valle de Guerra, Tejina and Orotava, with Telde and part of San Lorenzo being the main production centers of tomatoes on the Island of Gran Canaria.
Today this cultivation has spread to almost all towns of Tenerife and Gran Canaria, and is also found on the Island of La Palma in San Andrés and Sauces, Puntallana, Los Llanos and Garafia, being also cultivated on the island of La Gomera, in the Valle de Santiago, from the municipality of Alajeró, in that of Gran Rey de Arure and in the municipal term of Valle-Hermoso, also finding plantations of this solanaceous in Hermigua, Agulo and San Sebastián.
Where there is abundant water all year round, the banana crop is planted, and where irrigation is occasional, only the cultivation of the tomato or the potato is carried out, but especially the former.
To demonstrate the importance of this cultivation, it is sufficient to say that almost exclusively for the transport of these fruits from the Islands of La Palma and Gomera and from the southern ports to that of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, and to take the packaging materials to the production sites, there is a fleet of eight or ten small steamers that constantly make crossings for this purpose during the harvesting season.
Many farmers send their tomatoes directly to various European markets, England and Germany mainly; but due to the disappointments they have suffered with some fruit commission agents who exercise their industry in those markets, the custom of selling those fruits outright in the ports of these Islands and even in the producing towns is spreading.

aging them in

tween the fruits are filled with a mixture of sawdust and tur

Regarding
the use of the
residues of the
plants of group E, those of the pepper and the eggplant offer little importance, as they are reduced to the leaves
and stems, whose value is of little account.
Of the tomatoes, one must consider as residues those
unsuitable for shipment; for
although a small
quantity of the best of these residues is sold in the
markets of the province, this occurs only when
they are close to the important towns; the rest is
used in the feeding of livestock.
Passing over the meteorological accidents that af
fect the peppers and eggplants, due to the little importance
of their cultivation, it is appropriate to indicate that regarding the tomato, the conditions of heat and humidity are usually very favorable
for the development of Phytoptora
infestans, known by the name of mold. Conditions of heat and humidity favorable for the development
of Erysiphe polygoni are also often present, but the damage caused by this crypt
gama is less important than that of the former. Both are combated through treatments of lime and sulfur.
The winds sometimes cause some damage to the
tomatoes, reducing the harvests.
As for pests, it can be said that various species of the genus Pieris attack the tomato plants, among them
Pieris brassica, Pieris napi and Pieris rapae, which cause
